result.markdown: --- title: "South Yorkshire BRES job statistics 2015-2024" author: - name: "Dan Olner" format: html: output-file: "SouthYorkshire_BRESjobstats_201524" fig-width: 8 fig-height: 8 execute: echo: false message: false warning: false fig-responsive: false collapse: false navbar: false sidebar: false --- ::: {.cell} ::: ## Notes on the data This is: - [BRES](https://www.nomisweb.co.uk/datasets/newbres6pub) full time job count data at local authority level for 2015 to 2024 - 2 digit SIC sectors are used (shortened names) - Keeping only sectors with more than 1% of each local authority's total job count - Latest job values are the 2022-24 average, to smooth volatile jobs data - Tables are ordered by location quotient (LQ) to show which sectors are more concentrated in each local authority. E.g. Sheffield's top LQ sector is basic metals: its LQ of 5.13 = basic metals job count there is 5.1x higher than the Great Britain average. (BRES data is GB not UK.) - Compound Annual Growth Rate figures (just the year on year percent change taken from line-slopes through the data). Two are included: for the full 2015-2024 range, and for 2021-2024.
